RE-OWN-003.explanation: Tenancy by the entirety, which Virginia recognizes for spouses under Code 55.1-136, carries survivorship and cannot be severed by one spouse's deed alone; a severing deed must be signed by both spouses. A joint tenant, by contrast, can sever the joint tenancy by conveying a share alone.

RE-OWN-023.explanation: Under Virginia Code 55.1-407 an unrecorded deed is void as to a later purchaser for value without notice, so Buyer 2, who paid value, had no notice and recorded, prevails. Buyer 1's deed still binds the seller, who signed it.

RE-PROP-017.explanation: A section has 640 acres, so 640 / 4 = 160 acres for the SW 1/4, and 160 / 4 = 40 acres for the NE 1/4 of it. The 160-acre answer stops at the quarter section. The rectangular survey is on the national portion; Virginia land is described by metes and bounds and recorded plats.

RE-CON-026.explanation: Virginia Code 54.1-2139 allows dual agency only with the written consent of all parties, given after written disclosure of its consequences and before it begins. Telling only the seller leaves the buyer unaware of the divided loyalty.

RE-CON-027.explanation: In designated agency, Virginia Code 54.1-2139.1, the broker assigns separate licensees to each client within the same firm, and the supervising broker is the one treated as a dual agent. Subagency involves a cooperating licensee working for the seller through the listing broker.

RE-CON-037.explanation: Virginia Code 54.1-2131(B) requires a seller's licensee to disclose in writing to prospective buyers all material adverse facts about the property's physical condition that the licensee actually knows, whatever the seller instructs. Waiting for a buyer to ask is not enough.

RE-CON-039.explanation: Customers are owed honesty, and Virginia Code 54.1-2131(B) requires a seller's licensee to disclose known material adverse facts about the property's physical condition, even without an agency relationship. Loyalty and the other client duties belong only to the client.

RE-CON-040.explanation: Virginia Code 54.1-2138(A) requires a licensee who has a substantive discussion about a property with an unrepresented buyer to disclose whom she represents, in writing no later than when specific real estate assistance is first provided. Collecting his maximum price first would let him reveal information she must share with her client.

RE-CON-035.explanation: Virginia Code 54.1-2131(A)(3) requires a seller's licensee to keep the client's personal and financial information confidential unless the seller consents in writing. A seller's willingness to take less is not a material fact about the property, so it need not be disclosed.

RE-CON-002.explanation: Only the owner makes a promise, and the broker earns the fee only by performing, so the contract is unilateral. A bilateral contract needs a promise from each side. In Virginia a brokerage agreement must also be in writing under Code 54.1-2137(C).

RE-PRAC-005.question: A salesperson works as an independent contractor for a Virginia brokerage. Who is responsible for supervising the salesperson's real estate activities?
RE-PRAC-005.explanation: A Virginia salesperson may act only under the principal broker (or a supervising broker the principal broker designates), who must supervise the salesperson's activities under Board regulations 18VAC135-20-165 and -330. Independent contractor status is a tax classification and does not remove that duty.

RE-PRAC-003.explanation: Commingling is mixing client or customer funds with the broker's own money, and Board regulation 18VAC135-20-181(D) lists it as improper maintenance of escrow funds. Conversion is the more serious act of actually using those funds for the broker's own purposes.

excluded.RE-OWN-004: Community property: Virginia is not a community property state.
excluded.RE-OWN-021: Hypothetical 12-year adverse possession period; Virginia's period for recovery of land is 15 years, so the number could mislead.
excluded.RE-CON-028: Transaction broker or facilitator status does not exist in Virginia law; the nonagency option there is an independent contractor under a written brokerage agreement (Code 54.1-2130).
excluded.RE-CON-029: Subagency through the MLS: Code 54.1-2141 says using a common source information company creates no brokerage relationship, so the subagent framing misleads.
excluded.RE-CON-032: Agency by ratification: Code 54.1-2130 and 54.1-2137(B) require a written brokerage agreement before brokerage services, and the common law is abrogated where inconsistent (54.1-2144).
excluded.RE-CON-033: Listing terminated by the seller's death: Code 54.1-2137(A) lists the termination events for Virginia brokerage relationships and does not include death, so the keyed rule is not the statute's.
excluded.RE-CON-022: Earnest money dispute: Code 54.1-2108.2(3) gives Virginia brokers a release path under clear contract terms with 15-day notice; covered by REVA-VAESC-002 instead.
excluded.RE-PRAC-009: Net listing keyed as lawful: Board regulation 18VAC135-20-280(A)(5) makes a net listing an improper financial transaction in Virginia.
excluded.RE-PRAC-021: Vicarious liability of the broker: Board regulation 18VAC135-20-330 and Code 54.1-2142 limit broker responsibility to what the broker knew or should have known, so the keyed doctrine is too broad for Virginia.
excluded.RE-PRAC-002: Earnest money handling: the Virginia rule (fifth business banking day after ratification, Code 54.1-2108.2) is tested by REVA-VAESC-001.
excluded.RE-MATH-006: Assessment at 40% of market value; Virginia assesses real estate at fair market value (Constitution of Virginia, Art. X, sec. 2).
excluded.RE-VAL-028: Keys that assessments are often a fraction of market value; Virginia assesses at fair market value.
excluded.RE-PROP-024: Tax stated in mills on an assessed value; Virginia localities set rates per $100 of fair market value.
excluded.RE-MATH-016: Local transfer tax at $1.10 per $500; Virginia's grantor and recordation taxes use different rates, so the figure could mislead.
excluded.RE-DISC-015: Keys that disclosure forms vary by state; Virginia's buyer-beware statement (Code 55.1-703) is tested by REVA-VADSC items.
excluded.RE-DISC-018: Stigmatized property: Virginia's rule (Code 55.1-713(A)) is tested directly by REVA-VADSC-007.
excluded.RE-FIN-003: Lien-theory framing: Virginia uses deeds of trust with a trustee holding title, so a lien-theory mortgage item could confuse.
